preamble: Lenition of the voiceless postalveolar affricate [tʃ] to the voiced postalveolar fricative [ʒ] removes the stop closure and adds voicing in one step. Campidanese Sardinian shows this as a regular sandhi alternation. Word-initial voiceless stops and the affricate [p t tʃ k] are realized as voiced spirants [β ð ʒ ɣ] when a vowel-final word precedes them inside a phrase, so [tʃ] alternates with [ʒ] in the same word.

examples.note: After a vowel-final word in the same phrase, initial /tʃ/ surfaces as [ʒ]. It patterns with [tɛrːa] ~ [sa ðɛrːa] 'earth', and [kwatːru] ~ [dɛ ɣwatːru] 'four'. Chabot (2023) describes the pattern as systematic and exceptionless for the voiceless series.

sources: Chabot, A. (2023). Prosodic strength in Campidanese Sardinian as Substance-Free Phonology. Phonology (accepted manuscript, lingbuzz/007309). https://lingbuzz.net/lingbuzz/007309
